reconcile:fc7fc5bacd35c483aec31fe72ac969.text: Mic. 3, 5. Eth. ነሰከ id. Syr. by transp.
reconcile:fc7fc5bacd35c483aec31fe72ac969.note: The only difference between the readings is the order of the 2nd and 3rd Ethiopic letters. The 2nd printed glyph is a Π shape with a closed loop centred on its top bar, which is ሰ (sa). The 3rd glyph is a Π shape whose top has an open hook rising to the left, which is ከ (ka). That gives ነሰከ, the Ethiopic cognate of נשך 'to bite'. Reading 1 (ነከሰ) has these two letters swapped. All the Latin text matches in every reading.

reconcile:6c1e336f5045263cf78b0cf61fb872.note: The readings differ only in a dagesh in the tav. Reading 1 has תָּ; readings 2 and 3 have תָ. At display size the tav seems to show an inner dot above the qamets. A tav after silent shewa (כְ following holam-vav) is expected to take dagesh lene, which supports נוֹכְתָּא.
